_evidence: 0x0055616f walks the 0x160-byte ring records at 0x8943a0 from the start [0x866ec0] + 1 record ('mov edi,[0x866ec0]; add edi,0x160'): per record eax = dword +0x2c of the previous record ('[edi-0x134]') xor its own +0x2c; when nonzero, each of the dwords +0x30/+0x34/+0x38/+0x40/+0x3c that lacks some of those bits ('and edx,eax; cmp edx,eax; je') gets them ORed in; then 'add edi,0x160; cmp edi,[0x866eb8]; jne' - a do-while that stops only on equality, so the end lies at least two records above the start (end = start + 1 record would be passed and never met). Start records 0..3 (as segs_00558d9b) and end records 5..26 (segs_00558d9b's end 4 with start 3 walks off the array). Records 0..26: +0x2c from small bit sets {0,1,2,4,6,0x10,0x30,0x44,0x80,0xff} so neighbours are equal (je skip) or differ in a few bits, and the five target dwords from {0,1,2,3,6,7,0x10,0x30,0x44,0xc4,0xffffffff} so 'already has every changed bit' is true for some and false for other records (random dwords would make it true with probability ~2^-16). The ring records are zero in the image.
